title: How to make good pixel art effects with Claude
author: HugoDzz
selftext:
[Detailed write-up + code](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude). I’ve been messing around Claude for code-driven pixel art visual effects, here’s my learning so far:  


* Treat code as clay, form your ideas on the go instead of aim for a one-shot. Ask your agent to generate many option as video records, then pick one, and repeat until it feels right.
* Just trust your eyes, if something looks off, *make the effort* to go on the round trips with the LLM, the quality bar is on you.
* Learn from 3D (Houdini in my case), films etc. they are *very* good reference to learn from. Play games with great VFX as well, for instance Path of Exile 2 is an insanely good ref.

  
PS: I’ve also put a bunch of effects source code files together in the write-up, feel free to take them as reference or feed them as context to your LLM.

comments.author: miomidas
comments.body: Looks cool! Any game youre developing along with it?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Yes! The bosses VFX for the coop mode of Destroy Any Website game!

comments.author: mannrich
comments.body: What about the usage of the tokens? This is sustainable?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: So far it is pretty sustainable (Claude Opus 5.5 on Max plan); I've never ran into a token limit yet! And I can do back and forth for pretty long haha

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body: Thanks dude , I will try this out tomorrow!!

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Let me know how it goes! So far in my work, the library as context is a pretty solid setup!

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Have you done some stress tests for comparing sprite atlas based animations vs code based pixel animations by any chance ? 

Curious to know what the cpu cost difference would be If you let loose on 1000 effect nodes o.o

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Performance-wise, a sprite sheet will definitely be lighter, though I never ran into performance issue so far with this code-based FX approach (for pixel art). Also, a thing you can do as well is to render them as... sprites sheets! The Factorio-way: render the actual animation, and use plain PNGs.

replies.body: I will definitely have a look , thanks for sharing so much ! Scrolled passed a lot of them and their really good quality:)

replies.body: Thanks! Yeah, I'm very picky for everything pixel art, so I'm willing to spend a lot of time making them!

replies.author: HugoDzz

comments.author: albertyto
comments.body:
This is nice! Gotta say that I've been working on something similar(poe2 fan), not this detailed, for my game after I saw your scene post a few weeks ago, along with the surge of everyone doing pixel art.

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Yeah, it’s a steering work, basically technical art is becoming a communication and art direction work!

replies.author: HugoDzz

comments.author: crypticevincar
comments.body: I totally agree with your bullet points. Working on a pixel game right now too and making sure it stays in the theme is important. "I want this, I want it to look like this and do this when that happens. Make it something." It shows me a mockup and I can adjust it from there.

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Yeah!! It is really a clay work, I’m a programmer by day but I’d even say that it doesn’t matter that much (it helps for spotting bad designs and optimize stuff), going through that clay forming work is the true work!
